# Motion.page Desktop MCP

The Desktop MCP server exposes tools that let you create and manipulate animations directly in the Motion.page Desktop app. No code writing needed — you call tools, the builder updates live.

**Package:** `@motion.page/desktop-mcp`

```bash
claude mcp add motionpage-desktop-mcp -- npx @motion.page/desktop-mcp
```

---

## Workflow

1. **Orient** — call `get_builder_state` to see the current project, loaded timeline, and connection status
2. **Create** — call `create_timeline` with name, trigger, and animations in one call
3. **Refine** — use `add_animation`, `update_animation`, `set_trigger` to iterate
4. **Verify** — call `preview_code` to see the generated SDK code

The Desktop app must be running for full functionality. If disconnected, introspection tools still work in-memory.

---

## Tool Tiers

### Tier 1 — High-Level (80% of use cases)

Use these for most tasks. They handle validation, unit conversion, and auto-saving.

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `create_timeline` | Create a complete timeline with name, trigger, and animated nodes in one call |
| `add_animation` | Add an element with animation to an existing timeline (atomic, no broken states) |
| `update_animation` | Update from/to/duration/ease/stagger/split/fit/repeat on an existing node |
| `set_trigger` | Set or change trigger type and options |

### Tier 2 — Fine-Tuning

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `set_property` | Set a single animation property on a node |
| `remove_property` | Remove a property (reverts to element's natural CSS) |

### Tier 3 — Introspection (read-only)

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `get_builder_state` | Current state snapshot — start here |
| `list_timelines` | All timelines in the project |
| `get_timeline` | Full timeline details including generated code |
| `list_projects` | All projects (for switching) |
| `list_triggers` | Available trigger types with descriptions |
| `list_properties` | All animatable properties by category |
| `list_easings` | All easing functions with recommendations |
| `preview_code` | Generate SDK code without saving |

---

## Common Patterns

### Fade-in on page load

```
create_timeline({
  name: "Hero Entrance",
  trigger: { type: "pageLoad" },
  animations: [{
    selector: ".hero-title",
    from: { opacity: 0, y: 50 },
    duration: 0.8,
    ease: "power3.out"
  }]
})
```

### Scroll-triggered reveal

```
create_timeline({
  name: "Section Reveal",
  trigger: { type: "scroll", options: { scrub: true, start: "top 80%", end: "top 20%" } },
  animations: [{
    selector: ".card",
    from: { opacity: 0, y: 40, scale: 0.95 },
    duration: 0.6,
    ease: "power2.out"
  }]
})
```

### Hover effect

```
create_timeline({
  name: "Button Hover",
  trigger: { type: "hover", options: { target: ".btn" } },
  animations: [{
    selector: ".btn",
    to: { scale: 1.05, backgroundColor: "#0099ff" },
    duration: 0.3,
    ease: "power2.out"
  }]
})
```

### Staggered entrance

```
create_timeline({
  name: "List Stagger",
  trigger: { type: "pageLoad" },
  animations: [{
    selector: ".list-item",
    from: { opacity: 0, x: -30 },
    duration: 0.5,
    ease: "power3.out",
    stagger: { each: 0.1, from: "start" }
  }]
})
```

### Split text animation

```
create_timeline({
  name: "Text Reveal",
  trigger: { type: "pageLoad" },
  animations: [{
    selector: ".headline",
    from: { opacity: 0, y: 100 },
    duration: 0.8,
    ease: "power3.out",
    split: "chars",
    stagger: 0.03
  }]
})
```

---

## Trigger Types

| Type | Description | Key Options |
|------|-------------|-------------|
| `pageLoad` | Plays on page load (default) | timing |
| `pageExit` | Plays on navigation away | mode, selectors |
| `scroll` | Linked to scroll position | scrub, pin, start, end, snap, markers |
| `hover` | Plays on mouseenter | target, onLeave (reverse/pause/none) |
| `click` | Plays on click | target, toggle (reverse/restart/play) |
| `mouseMove` | Responds to mouse position | type (distance/axis), smooth |
| `gesture` | Touch/pointer/wheel gestures | types, presentation |
| `cursor` | Custom cursor follower | type (basic/text/media), smooth |

---

## Animation Properties

**Transform:** x, y, z, scale, scaleX, scaleY, rotate, rotateX, rotateY, skewX, skewY, transformOrigin
**Appearance:** opacity, backgroundColor, color, borderColor
**Dimensions:** width, height
**Filter:** CSS filter string (e.g. `"blur(10px)"`)
**Background:** backgroundPosition

---

## Easing

**Recommended:** `power2.out` (subtle) · `power3.out` (punchy) · `back.out` (playful) · `elastic.out` (spring) · `bounce.out` (bouncy)

All families: power1-4, sine, expo, circ, back, elastic, bounce — each with `.in`, `.out`, `.inOut` variants. Use `"none"` for linear.

---

## Timing Guidelines

| Duration | Use Case |
|----------|----------|
| 0.2–0.4s | Micro-interactions (hover, click feedback) |
| 0.5–0.8s | Element entrances |
| 0.8–1.5s | Dramatic reveals, hero animations |
| 1.5–3.0s | Slow, cinematic effects |

---

## Input Format

Tier 1 tools accept clean values — the server handles unit conversion automatically:

- `y: 50` → uses default unit (%)
- `x: "100px"` → explicit unit from CSS string
- `scale: 0.8` → unitless
- `filter: "blur(10px)"` → parsed into builder filter array

---

## Best Practices

1. **Start with `get_builder_state`** — always orient yourself before making changes
2. **Use `create_timeline` for new animations** — one call creates everything
3. **Use `preview_code` to verify** — check the generated SDK output before moving on
4. **Use Tier 1 tools first** — drop to Tier 2 only for surgical edits
5. **Use `from` only for reveals** — the builder resolves `to` from the element's natural CSS (opacity: 1, y: 0, etc.)
